statement: When an export re-presents a scorer's numbers, test whether any input behind each number was measured, not only whether the number is non-null. 2026-11-10, #709: the GitLab metrics export had to write no line for a value Cejel did not measure. The schema's nulls covered only an abstained report, but the scorer averages a category whose criteria are all insufficient_data or not_applicable to 0, and the overall score is 0 when nothing was measured, so a null check alone would have published real-looking zeros that GitLab then shows as score changes. The trading rubric added a second case: its codeTrustScore and processTrustScore are its first two categories under other names. Fix: write a trust line only when its named category has a measured criterion, and the overall line only when some criterion was measured; a criterion actually scored 0 is still written.
